answer: A farm's clones share one solver, so their past answers are interchangeable skins - none has a private history. Self-history interrogation: pick one earlier answer of this identity at random, like a raven returning to its roost, and demand a continuation - name the alternative it rejected, then extend its mechanism one step under a constraint revealed only now. A real author climbs from its own record toward a zenith it can retrace; a clone stalls or contradicts itself publicly. Cost grows per clone - a dossier plus bespoke reasoning for each - and no gale of templates carries them all.
